questions.question: In Shakespeare's 'The Merchant of Venice', which character delivers the celebrated speech on 'the quality of mercy' in the court of Venice?
questions.explanation: Portia disguised as the young lawyer Balthazar appeals for mercy in Act 4 Scene 1.

questions.question: Which character in Shakespeare's romance 'The Tempest' speaks the famous line 'O brave new world, that has such people in it'?
questions.explanation: Miranda speaks these amazed words upon seeing mankind for the first time in Act 5 Scene 1.

questions.question: In Shakespeare's tragedy 'Macbeth', which forest must advance toward Dunsinane hill before Macbeth can be vanquished according to the apparition?
questions.explanation: The third apparition prophesies Macbeth will never vanquish until Birnam Wood moves to Dunsinane.

questions.question: Convert the sentence into correct indirect speech: He said to her, 'Where do you live?'
options: He told her where did she live.
He asked her where she lived.
He inquired of her where did she live.
He asked her that where she lived.
questions.explanation: In indirect wh-questions, no coordinating that is used and word order becomes affirmative.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of the exclamatory sentence: The boy said, 'Hurrah! We have won the match.'
options: The boy exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
The boy exclaimed with sorrow that they won the match.
The boy told with delight that they have won the match.
The boy said with joy that we have won the match.
questions.explanation: Hurrah changes to exclaimed with joy, followed by past perfect tense.

questions.question: How many sonnets in total did William Shakespeare compose, as first collected and published in the 1609 quarto edition by Thomas Thorpe?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare collection consists of 154 sonnets followed by A Lover Complaint.

questions.question: Which contemporary dramatist paid tribute to Shakespeare in the 1623 First Folio with the words 'He was not of an age, but for all time'?
questions.explanation: Ben Jonson composed the famous dedicatory poem To the Memory of My Beloved Master William Shakespeare.

questions.question: Which lyrical drama by P.B. Shelley was written as a poetic sequel to Aeschylus's lost tragedy, celebrating the triumph of love and liberty?
questions.explanation: Prometheus Unbound in four acts represents Shelley philosophical masterpiece of human liberation.

questions.question: Select the correct indirect speech: The doctor said to the patient, 'Take this medicine twice daily.'
options: The doctor advised the patient to take that medicine twice daily.
The doctor told to the patient that he should take this medicine twice daily.
The doctor suggested the patient that take that medicine twice daily.
The doctor ordered the patient taking this medicine twice daily.
questions.explanation: Medical advice takes advised followed by infinitive to take, and this changes to that.

questions.question: What is the exact antonym of the word 'CANDID'?
questions.explanation: Candid means frank and honest; its opposite is deceitful or evasive.

questions.question: 'Our sweetest songs are those that tell of saddest thought' is an immortal line from which lyric by P.B. Shelley?
questions.explanation: Shelley pens this reflection on human existence in his 1820 poem To a Skylark.

questions.question: In his prose essay 'A Defence of Poetry', P.B. Shelley famously concluded that poets are the:
options: divine interpreters of nature and truth
questions.explanation: Shelley ends his famous 1821 essay by proclaiming poets as the unacknowledged legislators.

questions.question: Which ode by John Keats concludes with the enigmatic lines ''Beauty is truth, truth beauty,'—that is all / Ye know on earth, and all ye need to know'?
questions.explanation: Keats concludes Ode on a Grecian Urn with this renowned aesthetic aphorism.

questions.question: Choose the most appropriate synonym for the word 'METICULOUS':
questions.explanation: Meticulous implies showing great attention to detail, matching painstaking.

questions.question: Select the correct antonym of the word 'OBSOLETE':
questions.explanation: Obsolete means no longer produced or used; its antonym is contemporary or current.

questions.question: Which romantic narrative poem by John Keats, composed in Spenserian stanzas, recounts the love of Porphyro and Madeline?
options: Isabella; or, The Pot of Basil
questions.explanation: The Eve of St. Agnes written in 1819 is based on the medieval folklore of St. Agnes Eve.

questions.question: In which city and year did John Keats die of tuberculosis at the young age of twenty-five?
questions.explanation: Keats died on 23 February 1821 in Rome and was buried in the Protestant Cemetery.

questions.question: Alfred Lord Tennyson's monumental elegy 'In Memoriam A.H.H.' was composed in deep sorrow over the sudden death of which Cambridge companion?
questions.explanation: Tennyson spent seventeen years writing In Memoriam after Arthur Henry Hallam died in 1833.

questions.question: Which of the following words is the closest synonym of 'PRAGMATIC'?
questions.explanation: Pragmatic means dealing with matters sensibly and realistically, meaning practical.

questions.question: Find the correct antonym of the word 'TACITURN':
questions.explanation: Taciturn describes someone reserved or uncommunicative; loquacious means very talkative.

questions.question: Which poem by Alfred Tennyson, inspired by an episode in Homer's 'Odyssey', portrays mariners succumbing to an enchanted languor?
questions.explanation: The Lotos-Eaters depicts Ulysses weary mariners choosing sweet indolence over home.

questions.question: Pip, Miss Havisham, and the escaped convict Abel Magwitch are central characters in which celebrated Charles Dickens novel?
questions.explanation: Great Expectations published in 1861 follows Pip moral education and development.

questions.question: Which satirical novel by Charles Dickens opens with Thomas Gradgrind insisting upon 'Facts. Teach these boys and girls nothing but Facts'?
questions.explanation: Hard Times in 1854 critiques utilitarianism in the fictional industrial town of Coketown.

questions.question: Choose the option that clarifies the distinction between 'PRINCIPAL' and 'PRINCIPLE':
options: Principal means a moral rule; principle means the chief person in authority.
Both words mean an established moral doctrine or philosophy.
Both words denote the primary sum of money invested in finance.
Principal means head of an institution; principle means a fundamental truth or rule.
questions.explanation: Principal is head or main capital; principle is a core moral rule or law.

questions.question: A person who has a great love for and collects books is called a:
questions.explanation: A bibliophile is an enthusiastic collector or lover of books.

questions.question: What is the explanatory subtitle given to William Wordsworth's epic autobiographical poem 'The Prelude'?
questions.explanation: The Prelude was published posthumously in 1850 subtitled Growth of a Poet Mind.

questions.question: 'The Child is father of the Man' is a famous philosophical line found in which lyrical poem by William Wordsworth?
questions.explanation: The line occurs in My Heart Leaps Up and was later used as epigraph to the Immortality Ode.

questions.question: In which year did William Wordsworth accept the official appointment of Poet Laureate of the United Kingdom following Robert Southey?
questions.explanation: Wordsworth accepted the Poet Laureateship in 1843 after Robert Southey passed away.

questions.question: One who holds a deep hatred or distrust of humankind is known as a:
questions.explanation: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes humanity; philanthropist loves humanity.

questions.question: An author's text or book before it has been printed is called a:
questions.explanation: Manuscript literally means written by hand, denoting an unpublished text.

questions.question: Which famous line opens T.S. Eliot's landmark dramatic monologue 'The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock'?
options: Let us go then, you and I
Here I am, an old man in a dry month
Because I do not hope to turn again
questions.explanation: Prufrock published in 1915 opens with Let us go then, you and I, when the evening is spread out.

questions.question: In which year was T.S. Eliot awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature for his outstanding, pioneer contribution to present-day poetry?
questions.explanation: Eliot received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1948 as well as the Order of Merit.

questions.question: Charles Lamb co-authored the timeless children's adaptation 'Tales from Shakespeare' (1807) alongside which collaborator?
questions.explanation: Charles Lamb wrote the tragedies while his sister Mary Lamb wrote the comedies.

questions.question: A mournful poem composed to lament the death of someone revered or beloved is called an:
questions.explanation: An elegy is a reflective poem of lament for the dead.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'a wild goose chase'?
options: A fast race between skilled competitors
A foolish and fruitless search or pursuit
A journey undertaken without careful planning
questions.explanation: A wild goose chase signifies pursuing something unattainable or hopeless.

questions.question: In which essay of Elia does Charles Lamb express tender sympathy and affection for the young climbing boys of the chimney sweeping trade?
questions.explanation: Lamb praises chimney sweeps in this delightful essay first published in London Magazine.

questions.question: Michael Henchard, who impulsively sells his wife Susan and infant child at a fair, is the tragic protagonist of which Thomas Hardy novel?
questions.explanation: Henchard is the titular character in The Mayor of Casterbridge published in 1886.

questions.question: Which was Thomas Hardy's final completed novel whose harsh critical reception caused him to abandon novel writing altogether?
questions.explanation: The public scandal over Jude the Obscure in 1895 led Hardy to dedicate himself solely to poetry.

questions.question: What does the idiomatic phrase 'to bite the bullet' mean?
options: To chew on hard objects when feeling nervous
To show cowardice in the presence of danger
To engage in fierce military combat
To face a difficult or painful situation with grim courage
questions.explanation: It refers to enduring an unavoidable painful experience bravely.

questions.question: The phrase 'at the eleventh hour' means:
options: At an inconvenient time of the day
Late in the evening near midnight
At the latest possible moment before a deadline
Early in the morning before business begins
questions.explanation: From the biblical parable of the labourers, it means at the last possible moment.

questions.question: Which poem by Robert Frost opens with the iconic lines 'Two roads diverged in a yellow wood, / And sorry I could not travel both'?
questions.explanation: The Road Not Taken was published as the opening poem of Mountain Interval in 1916.

questions.question: How many Pulitzer Prizes for Poetry did Robert Frost win over the course of his distinguished career?
questions.explanation: Frost remains the only poet to win four Pulitzer Prizes for Poetry.

questions.question: 'I am Indian, very brown, born in Malabar, / I speak three languages, write in two, dream in one' are lines from which poem by Kamala Das?
questions.explanation: These assertive autobiographical lines occur in Kamala Das signature poem An Introduction.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the appropriate preposition: The father is blind ______ the vices of his favourite son.
questions.explanation: When blind means unwilling to see or notice faults, it is followed by preposition to.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He has been suffering from acute malaria ______ last Tuesday.
questions.explanation: A specific point in time in the past taking present perfect continuous takes since.

questions.question: Munoo, an innocent hill boy who endures relentless suffering as a domestic servant, factory worker, and rickshaw puller, is the protagonist of which novel?
questions.explanation: Coolie published in 1936 portrays Munoo tragic death from tuberculosis in Simla.

questions.question: Frederic Henry, an American ambulance driver serving on the Italian front, falls in love with Catherine Barkley in which Ernest Hemingway novel?
options: Across the River and into the Trees
questions.explanation: A Farewell to Arms in 1929 is Hemingway semi-autobiographical World War I novel.

questions.question: Which collection of poems by Nissim Ezekiel won the prestigious Sahitya Akademi Award in 1983?
questions.explanation: Latter-Day Psalms published in 1982 earned Ezekiel the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1983.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: We congratulated her ______ her outstanding achievement in the examination.
questions.explanation: The standard grammatical usage is to congratulate someone on something.

questions.question: Which negative prefix is correctly added to the adjective 'LEGIBLE' to indicate that writing cannot be read?
questions.explanation: Words beginning with l like legible take the negative prefix il- forming illegible.

questions.question: Walt Whitman's masterpiece poem 'Song of Myself' was first published without a title in the historic 1855 edition of:
questions.explanation: Song of Myself formed the centerpiece of the original twelve poems of Leaves of Grass in 1855.

questions.question: Which 1929 novel by William Faulkner portrays the tragic decline of the Compson family using four distinct narrative viewpoints?
questions.explanation: The Sound and the Fury takes its title from Macbeth and employs stream of consciousness.

questions.question: In Chaucer's 'The Canterbury Tales', which pilgrim is chosen by lot to tell the first tale on the road to Canterbury?
questions.explanation: The Knight draws the shortest cut at the Tabard Inn and begins the storytelling contest.

questions.question: Which suffix is attached to the root of 'BRIEF' to form an abstract noun signifying shortness in speech or writing?
questions.explanation: The root forms the abstract noun brevity with the suffix -ity.

questions.question: What is the proper negative prefix for the adjective 'RATIONAL'?
questions.explanation: Words starting with r standardly take the negative prefix ir- to form irrational.

questions.question: Geoffrey Chaucer composed his literary works in which Middle English regional dialect, establishing it as the literary standard?
questions.explanation: Chaucer London English was part of the East Midland dialect of Middle English.

questions.question: Maggie Tulliver and her brother Tom are the central figures whose relationship ends tragically in the flood in which George Eliot novel?
questions.explanation: The Mill on the Floss published in 1860 follows Maggie Tulliver spiritual struggle on the River Floss.

questions.question: In George Eliot's novel 'Silas Marner', what is the name of the gold-haired orphan girl who transforms the solitary weaver's life?
questions.explanation: Eppie wanders into Silas hearth on New Year Eve replacing his stolen hoard of gold.

questions.question: Identify the grammatically correct sentence from the options below:
options: One of the student was awarded a scholarship.
One of the students was awarded a scholarship.
One of the student were awarded a scholarship.
One of the students were awarded a scholarship.
questions.explanation: One of takes a plural noun followed by a singular verb.

questions.question: Transform the sentence by removing the adverb 'too': 'He is too old to run fast.'
options: He is very old and cannot run fast.
He is too old so he cannot run fast.
He is so old that he could not run fast.
He is so old that he cannot run fast.
questions.explanation: Too... to transforms into so... that plus cannot when the principal verb is in present tense.

questions.question: Which upright farmer chooses the gallows rather than sign a false confession in Arthur Miller's play 'The Crucible'?
questions.explanation: John Proctor tears up his confession to preserve his integrity and name in Act 4.

questions.question: In Arthur Miller's 1947 play 'All My Sons', which character is revealed to have shipped defective aircraft parts during the war?
questions.explanation: Joe Keller prioritized factory profits over pilot safety, causing twenty-one plane crashes.

questions.question: Pecola Breedlove, a young African-American girl who yearns for white beauty ideals, is the protagonist of Toni Morrison's debut novel:
questions.explanation: The Bluest Eye published in 1970 was Toni Morrison groundbreaking first novel.

questions.question: Transform the positive degree sentence into comparative degree: 'No other dramatist in England is as great as Shakespeare.'
options: Shakespeare is greater than any other dramatist in England.
Shakespeare was greater than any dramatist in England.
Shakespeare is great than all dramatists in England.
Shakespeare is the most great dramatist in England.
questions.explanation: Positive no other... as transforms into comparative greater than any other.

questions.question: Select the sentence with correct inversion following the negative adverb 'Hardly':
options: Hardly had the train arrived when the crowd rushed forward.
Hardly had the train arrived then the crowd rushed forward.
Hardly did the train arrived when the crowd rushed forward.
Hardly the train had arrived than the crowd rushed forward.
questions.explanation: Hardly requires auxiliary inversion had before the subject and pairs with when.

questions.question: Milkman Dead embarks on a quest to uncover his ancestral heritage in which 1977 novel by Toni Morrison?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon won the National Book Critics Circle Award and established Morrison renown.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech in Macbeth's famous declaration: 'Life's but a walking shadow, a poor player...'
questions.explanation: An implicit identification of life with a walking shadow and an actor is a metaphor.

questions.question: What figure of speech is exemplified by expressing an affirmative statement by negating its contrary, as in 'He is no mean scholar'?
questions.explanation: Litotes is an understatement in which an affirmative is expressed by negating its opposite.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct subject-verb agreement with 'as well as'?
options: The captain, as well as the crew members, have been saved.
The captain, as well as the crew members, was saved.
The captain, as well as the crew members, were saved.
The captain, as well as the crew members, are saved.
questions.explanation: Parenthetical expressions introduced by as well as agree with the first subject.

questions.question: Choose the correct passive voice of the imperative sentence: 'Shut the window.'
options: You are ordered to shut the window.
The window should be shut by someone.
questions.explanation: Imperative commands are standardly transformed into passive using Let plus object plus be shut.

questions.question: Expressions such as 'open secret', 'sweet sorrow', and 'wise fool' are examples of which figure of speech?
questions.explanation: An oxymoron juxtaposes two contradictory words or terms side by side.

questions.question: 'I wandered lonely as a cloud' in William Wordsworth's celebrated poem 'Daffodils' is an example of:
questions.explanation: An explicit comparison between two dissimilar things using as or like constitutes a simile.

questions.question: Which figure of speech is present in the sentence 'United we stand, divided we fall'?
questions.explanation: Antithesis balances two contrasting ideas within a parallel grammatical construction.

questions.question: Change the passive sentence into active voice: 'By whom was this exquisite poem written?'
options: Who has written this exquisite poem?
Who had written this exquisite poem?
questions.explanation: By whom was... written changes into the active interrogative Who wrote.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly employs the conjunction 'lest':
options: Walk carefully lest you will fall.
Walk carefully lest you may not fall.
Walk carefully lest you should not fall.
Walk carefully lest you should fall.
questions.explanation: Lest expresses negative purpose and must be followed by should without another negative.

questions.question: Which critic introduced the influential phrase 'dissociation of sensibility' in his 1921 essay 'The Metaphysical Poets'?
questions.explanation: Eliot argued that seventeenth-century poets could feel their thought as immediately as the odor of a rose.

questions.question: In 'Preface to Shakespeare' (1765), which critic defended Shakespeare against neoclassical critics for neglecting the unities of time and place?
questions.explanation: Dr. Johnson observed that the spectators at a theatre never lose their senses and understand dramatic illusion.

questions.question: Which ancient critical treatise, traditionally attributed to Longinus, outlines the five principal sources of transport and elevation in writing?
questions.explanation: Peri Hypsous or On the Sublime examines the sublime nature of great literature.

questions.question: Identify the word that is correctly spelled:
questions.explanation: Lieutenant is spelled with l-i-e-u-t-e-n-a-n-t.

questions.question: Select the option with the correct spelling:
questions.explanation: Separate is spelled with an a in the second syllable s-e-p-a-r-a-t-e.

questions.question: In 'Biographia Literaria' (1817), S.T. Coleridge famously distinguished between which two faculties of the poetic mind?
questions.explanation: Coleridge defined primary imagination as universal human perception and secondary as conscious poetic creation.

questions.question: What is the critical term for the elaborate, far-fetched metaphors and comparisons characteristic of seventeenth-century metaphysical poets like John Donne?
questions.explanation: Metaphysical conceits draw surprising analogies between spiritual concepts and physical realities.

questions.question: The English Elizabethan era is historically defined by the reign of Queen Elizabeth I across which date range?
questions.explanation: Queen Elizabeth I reigned from November 1558 until her death in March 1603.

questions.question: Identify the correct British English spelling:
questions.explanation: British English preserves the classical digraph in manoeuvre.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled word from the following:
questions.explanation: Privilege has two i vowels and no d, spelled p-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e.

questions.question: The mid-to-late eighteenth-century literary transition preceding the Romantic revival is frequently designated as:
questions.explanation: The period between 1745 and 1798 is commonly known as the Age of Sensibility or Age of Johnson.

questions.question: A standard poetic line containing five metrical feet with an unstressed syllable followed by a stressed syllable in each foot is called:
questions.explanation: Iambic pentameter is the preeminent meter of blank verse and English sonnets.

questions.question: A lyric poem consisting of exactly fourteen lines, traditionally divided into octave and sestet or three quatrains and a couplet, is a:
questions.explanation: A sonnet is a fourteen-line poetic form developed by Petrarch and perfected in English by Shakespeare.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that is correctly punctuated:
options: John Keats the English poet, died in Rome.
John Keats the English poet died, in Rome.
John Keats, the English poet, died in Rome.
John Keats, the English poet died in Rome.
questions.explanation: The appositive phrase the English poet must be enclosed between commas.

questions.question: Identify the grammatical tense of the verb in: 'He had been waiting for the bus for thirty minutes when it finally arrived.'
questions.explanation: Had been waiting denotes an action continuing in the past before another past event.
